title: Combining Transformations
short: Apply stretches, reflections and shifts in the right order.
trouble: Students shift before stretching inside the function, so 2(x − 3) is read as a shift of 6.

blocks.html: You already know each move on its own (Shifting and Stretching Graphs): $f(x) + k$ shifts up, $f(x - h)$ shifts right, $a f(x)$ stretches vertically and $f(-x)$ reflects across the $y$-axis. Now you will combine them into one formula and keep track of the order.

In $g(x) = a\,f\big(b(x - h)\big) + k$, the outside numbers act on outputs: multiply by $a$, then add $k$. The inside numbers act on inputs, backwards: divide by $b$, then add $h$. A point $(x, y)$ on $f$ lands at $\left(\frac{x}{b} + h,\ ay + k\right)$.

Follow one point. Outside, $g$ computes $f(\dots)$, multiplies by $a$ and adds $k$, in that order, just like the order of operations. Inside, $g$ needs to feed $f$ the same input as before. If $f$ had the point $(4, 2)$, then $g$ reaches that height when $b(x - h) = 4$. Solving for $x$ undoes the inside steps in reverse: $x = \frac{4}{b} + h$. That is why inside changes feel backwards.

blocks.name: transformfn

opts.task: Make g(x) = √(2(x − 3)): set b = 2 and h = 3.

blocks.cap: Start with $y = \sqrt{x}$. Set $b = 2$ and $h = 3$ to build $\sqrt{2(x - 3)} = \sqrt{2x - 6}$, and watch the starting point land at $x = 3$, not $x = 6$.

blocks.title: Reading a combined transformation
blocks.q: Describe how $g(x) = -2(x - 3)^2 + 1$ comes from $f(x) = x^2$, and find where the point $(1, 1)$ lands.
steps: Inside: $x - 3$ shifts the graph 3 to the right.
Outside: $-2$ reflects across the $x$-axis and stretches by 2; then $+1$ shifts up 1.
The point $(1, 1)$: the new $x$ solves $x - 3 = 1$, so $x = 4$. The new $y$ is $-2 \cdot 1 + 1 = -1$.
blocks.a: Reflect, stretch by 2, right 3, up 1; $(1, 1)$ lands at $(4, -1)$.

blocks.title: Factor the inside first
blocks.q: Where does the graph of $g(x) = \sqrt{2x - 6}$ start, and where does the point $(4, 2)$ of $\sqrt{x}$ land?
steps: Factor out the 2: $2x - 6 = 2(x - 3)$. So $b = 2$ (squeeze toward the $y$-axis by $\frac{1}{2}$) and $h = 3$.
The parent starts at $(0, 0)$. The new start solves $2(x - 3) = 0$: $x = 3$. So $g$ starts at $(3, 0)$.
For $(4, 2)$: solve $2(x - 3) = 4$, so $x - 3 = 2$ and $x = 5$. The height stays 2.

blocks.title: Writing the equation
blocks.q: Reflect $y = |x|$ across the $x$-axis, stretch it vertically by 3, then shift it 2 left and 4 down.
steps: Down 4: $y = -3|x + 2| - 4$. The vertex moved from $(0, 0)$ to $(-2, -4)$.

blocks.html: Reading $\sqrt{2x - 6}$ as a shift of 6. The 2 multiplies the whole inside, so factor it out: $2x - 6 = 2(x - 3)$, a shift of 3. Quick check: find where the inside equals 0. For $2x - 6 = 0$ that is $x = 3$, so the key point moved to $x = 3$.
